alt: Alberta register a business name page with the Types of business names section and the trade name description highlighted
caption: Read Alberta's Types of business names. A trade name is what you register when you do business under a name other than your own personal name.

alt: Alberta register a business name page with the step about getting a Business Name Report from NUANS highlighted
caption: Before you register, consider a NUANS Business Name Report. Alberta recommends one to find similar names, but it is optional and NUANS members charge for it.

alt: Alberta register a business name page with the Declaration of Trade Name form link highlighted
caption: Fill in the Declaration of Trade Name form before you visit a registry agent. Partnerships use a different form.

alt: Alberta find a business registry page with the level 1 basic registrations list and the note that service fees vary highlighted
caption: Find a registry agent that handles basic registrations, which include trade names. Service fees are not regulated and vary between agents, so ask for the total before you go.

alt: City of Calgary open a retail business page with online or phone sales and home-based retail sales highlighted in the list of businesses that need a licence
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Calgary, for example, lists online or phone sales and home-based retail sales among the businesses that need a licence. Look up your own city or town in the same way.

alt: Arizona Corporation Commission business services FAQ with the sentence giving the $85 online LLC filing fee highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, check the Articles of Organization fee with the Corporation Commission.

alt: Arizona Corporation Commission 10 steps page with the step on checking name availability opened and highlighted
caption: Check your business name against corporations, LLCs and trade names on the Corporation Commission's search.

alt: Arizona Corporation Commission 10 steps page with the sentence saying a trade name lasts 5 years and is registered by the Secretary of State highlighted
caption: Register a trade name with the Secretary of State, not the Corporation Commission. It lasts 5 years.

alt: Arizona Corporation Commission FAQ answer on publishing documents with the sentence about the publication letter highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, watch for the Commission's letter saying whether you must publish a notice.

alt: Arizona Corporation Commission FAQ answer saying LLCs are not required to file annual reports, highlighted
caption: Arizona LLCs do not file an annual report.

alt: Arizona Corporation Commission 10 steps page with the step on city or county taxes and business licensing opened and highlighted
caption: Register with your city, or your county if you are outside city limits, for any local business license.

alt: Name Request page with the action selector for starting a new business name
caption: Open Name Request and choose the action that matches what you're doing. For a new business, pick the option to get a business name.

alt: Name Request page with the How to Build Your Name guidance
caption: Read How to Build Your Name before you type anything. A name needs a distinctive part and a description, and it must not clash with an existing name.

alt: BC Registries and Online Services home page with the Create Account button highlighted
caption: Start at the BC Registries home page and choose Create Account.

alt: Create account page offering sign-in with BC Services Card
caption: Accounts are created with a BC Services Card. Have it set up before you start.

alt: Name Request page with the action selector
caption: Check and reserve your business name with Name Request before registering.

alt: eTaxBC log on page with the Enrol now option highlighted
caption: On the eTaxBC home page, use Enrol now to create an eTaxBC profile. You'll register for PST from inside your profile.

alt: California Secretary of State Name Reservations page with the Reserving a Name heading and the Business Search link highlighted
caption: Search your name in the Secretary of State Business Search first. It is only a preliminary check and does not cover county fictitious business names or trademarks.

alt: California Secretary of State LLC forms table with the Articles of Organization and Statement of Information rows highlighted
caption: Forming an LLC costs $70 for the Articles of Organization. The Statement of Information costs $20 and is due within 90 days, then every two years.

alt: Franchise Tax Board LLC page with the Annual Tax section and the $800 annual tax sentence highlighted
caption: Every California LLC also pays an $800 annual tax to the Franchise Tax Board, even in a year with no sales.

alt: CDTFA Publication 107 Applying for a Seller's Permit page with the no charge sentence highlighted
caption: The seller's permit is free. The CDTFA may ask for a security deposit depending on your type of business and expected sales.

alt: CDTFA sales and use tax rates page with the Tax Districts heading and the statewide rate sentence highlighted
caption: The statewide rate is 7.25%. Most areas add district taxes, so look up the rate for your address with the CDTFA tool on this page.

alt: CalGold permit assistance page with the Select a City and Select a Business Type fields highlighted
caption: Choose your city and type of business in CalGold to see the permits that may apply. Confirm each one with the agency listed.

alt: Chrome's Site settings page for an example site, with the site name and the Delete data button highlighted
caption: In Chrome, Site settings opens a page for the site you were on (1). Click Delete data (2), then confirm. This shot uses an example site.

alt: Florida Department of Revenue account registration page with the Register Online to Collect and Pay Taxes or Fees link highlighted
caption: Register online with the Florida Business Tax Application. You receive your certificate of registration and annual resale certificate.

alt: Florida Department of Revenue sales and use tax page with the 6% state rate and the Discretionary Sales Surtax heading highlighted
caption: Charge the 6% state rate plus the surtax for the county where the item is delivered.

alt: Georgia.gov starting a business guide with the Sole Proprietorship answer open and the sentence saying sole proprietorships are not registered highlighted
caption: Read Georgia.gov's note that a sole proprietorship is not registered with the Secretary of State.

alt: Georgia.gov Register an LLC page with the Register online section open and the $100 filing fee highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, check the Secretary of State filing fee before you decide.

alt: Georgia.gov annual registration for an LLC page with the April 1 deadline sentence highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, note the April 1 deadline for its annual registration.

alt: Georgia Department of Revenue sales and use tax registration FAQ with the answer on who must register highlighted
caption: Every dealer registers for a sales and use tax number, even if all sales are online.

alt: Georgia Department of Revenue page on who needs to collect sales tax with the out-of-state sales threshold question highlighted
caption: If you sell from outside Georgia, check the 200 sales or $100,000 threshold.

alt: Georgia Department of Revenue tax rates page with the sentence on which rate applies highlighted
caption: Charge the rate for the county where your customer takes delivery.

alt: Illinois DCEO Begin Here page with the Starting Your Business in Illinois Handbook link highlighted
caption: Read DCEO's Starting Your Business in Illinois Handbook to compare a sole proprietorship and an LLC.

alt: Illinois Department of Revenue Income Tax Rates page with the Individual Income Tax label highlighted
caption: Illinois taxes your business profit at a flat individual income tax rate.

alt: Cook County Clerk Assumed Business Name Registration page with the How to Apply text about the $50 fee highlighted
caption: County clerks file assumed names. Cook County, for example, takes applications online.

alt: Cook County Clerk page with the sentence about publishing the notice once a week for three consecutive weeks highlighted
caption: Publish the notice in a local newspaper once a week for three weeks, starting within 15 days.

alt: Cook County Clerk page with the sentence about submitting proof of publication within 50 days highlighted
caption: Return the newspaper's proof of publication to the clerk within 50 days.

alt: Illinois Department of Revenue Business Registration page with the MyTax Illinois link highlighted
caption: Register online with MyTax Illinois using Register a New Business (Form REG-1).

alt: Illinois Department of Revenue Business Registration page with the sentence about registering before any purchases or sales highlighted
caption: Register before you buy stock to resell or make any sales.

alt: Illinois Department of Revenue answer page with the 6.25 percent general merchandise rate highlighted
caption: The state rate is 6.25% on general merchandise. Local rates add to it.

alt: Indiana Department of Revenue business FAQ with the sentence that sole proprietorships need not register with the Secretary of State highlighted
caption: A sole proprietorship does not register with the Indiana Secretary of State.

alt: Indiana Department of Revenue rates page with the 2026 individual income tax rate highlighted
caption: Indiana's individual income tax rate is 2.95% for 2026, plus your county's income tax.

alt: Monroe County Recorder assumed business names page with the $25 recording fee highlighted
caption: Check your county recorder's fee for an assumed business name. Monroe County charges $25.

alt: Indiana Secretary of State business entity reports page with the every-other-year due date highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, file a business entity report every other year in the month it was formed.

alt: Indiana Department of Revenue sales tax page with the seven percent registration sentence highlighted
caption: Register with the Department of Revenue to collect Indiana's 7% sales tax.

alt: Indiana Department of Revenue remote sellers page with the $100,000 threshold highlighted
caption: Out-of-state sellers register once sales into Indiana exceed $100,000 in a calendar year.

alt: Indiana Business Owner's Guide with the sentence that Indiana has no single business license highlighted
caption: Indiana has no single general business license. Check state, county and city rules for what you sell.

alt: WhatIsMyIP.com home page with an example IPv4 address, its Copy button and the IPv6 address row highlighted
caption: Your IPv4 address is at the top (1). Click Copy beside it (2) to copy it. The row below (3) is your IPv6 address. If you see both, send both. This shot uses example addresses and hides the map.

alt: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 156C section 12 with the $500 certificate of organization and annual report fees highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, note that the certificate of organization and each annual report cost $500.

alt: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 156C section 3 with the rule on words an LLC name must contain highlighted
caption: Make sure an LLC name includes "LLC" or one of the other words the law lists.

alt: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 110 section 5 with the rule to file a business certificate with the city or town clerk highlighted
caption: File your business certificate with the clerk of each city or town where you have a business office. Ask the clerk for the current fee.

alt: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 110 section 5 with the four-year renewal rule highlighted
caption: Renew your business certificate every four years, or it lapses.

alt: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 64H section 2 with the 6.25 percent sales tax rate highlighted
caption: Charge the statewide 6.25% rate on taxable sales delivered in Massachusetts.

alt: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 64H section 34 with the $100,000 remote retailer threshold highlighted
caption: Sellers based outside Massachusetts must register once their sales into the state exceed $100,000 in the current or prior year.

alt: Manitoba choose your business structure page with the sole proprietorship section and the personal liability point highlighted
caption: Read Manitoba's guide to business structures. A sole proprietorship is the simplest way to start, but the owner is personally liable for all business debts.

alt: Manitoba Companies Office business names page with the link to information on choosing a business name highlighted
caption: Read the Companies Office guidelines for choosing a business name before you request a name reservation.

alt: Manitoba Companies Office business name forms and fees page with the Request for Name Reservation row highlighted
caption: Start with a Request for Name Reservation. It costs $45, and an approved name is held for 90 days.

alt: Manitoba Companies Office business name forms and fees page with the Business Name Registration row highlighted
caption: Then file the Business Name Registration. Filing online is fastest, and it costs $60 for three years.

alt: Manitoba Finance taxation page with the Sign up for TAXcess link and the Do I Need to Register link highlighted
caption: Check Do I Need to Register?, then sign up for TAXcess and register for a retail sales tax account. Registration is free.

alt: City of Winnipeg home-based business page with the sentence saying a home-based business development permit is required highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Winnipeg, for example, needs a home-based business development permit if business mail comes to your home or you do the paperwork there. Look up your own municipality in the same way.

alt: Maryland Business Express Choose a Business Structure page with the sole proprietorship description highlighted
caption: Read the Business Express description of a sole proprietorship, the simplest way to start.

alt: Maryland Business Express Select a Business Name page with the name search link highlighted
caption: Search your business name on Maryland Business Express before you commit to it.

alt: Maryland Business Express Register a Business page with the note that sole proprietors need an SDAT ID number highlighted
caption: Note that a sole proprietor still needs an SDAT ID number to open a business bank account.

alt: Maryland Business Express Select a Business Name page with the Register a Trade Name link highlighted
caption: If you use a name other than your own, register a trade name with your SDAT Department ID.

alt: Maryland Business Express tax accounts page with the Combined Registration Application explanation highlighted
caption: Register for your sales and use tax license with the Combined Registration Application.

alt: Maryland Business Express tax accounts page with the Sales and Use Tax License entry highlighted
caption: Check that the sales and use tax license is the account you need for selling goods in Maryland.

alt: Maryland Business Express licenses page with the trader's license description highlighted
caption: Read when Maryland requires a trader's license for selling goods.

alt: Maryland Business Express licenses page with the List of Circuit Court Clerks link highlighted
caption: Find your county's Clerk of the Circuit Court for the trader's license and local license questions.

alt: Michigan Legislature MCL 450.5101 LLC filing fees with the $50 articles of organization fee highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, note the filing fee. Articles of Organization cost $50.

alt: Michigan Legislature MCL 450.4204 with the rule that an LLC name must contain limited liability company, L.L.C. or L.C. highlighted
caption: Read the name rules before you form an LLC. The name must say it is a limited liability company.

alt: Michigan Legislature MCL 445.1 with the requirement to file an assumed name certificate with the county clerk highlighted
caption: File your assumed name certificate with the clerk of each county where you do business. Ask the clerk for the current fee.

alt: Michigan Legislature MCL 450.4207 with the February 15 annual statement deadline highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, file its annual statement with LARA by February 15 each year.

alt: Michigan Legislature MCL 205.52 General Sales Tax Act with the 6% rate highlighted
caption: Note the rate. Michigan sales tax is 6%, with no county or city sales taxes on top.

alt: Michigan Legislature MCL 205.52c with the $100,000 and 200 transactions thresholds for out-of-state sellers highlighted
caption: Sellers outside Michigan register once they pass $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions into Michigan in the previous calendar year.

alt: Missouri Secretary of State Starting a Business page with the sentence on sole proprietorships highlighted
caption: A sole proprietorship needs no filing with the Secretary of State, the simplest way to start.

alt: Missouri Secretary of State FAQ page with the online and paper LLC filing fees highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, filing the articles online costs less than filing on paper.

alt: Missouri Secretary of State fictitious name FAQ with the answer on the filing fee highlighted
caption: Register your fictitious name with the Secretary of State online or by mail with Form Corp. 56.

alt: Missouri Secretary of State fictitious name FAQ with the sentence on the five-year registration period highlighted
caption: The registration lasts five years. Renew it in the six months before it expires.

alt: Missouri Secretary of State FAQ page with the question on LLC annual reports highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, Missouri does not require an annual report.

alt: Missouri Department of Revenue business registration page with the Start Registration Here button highlighted
caption: Apply online for your retail sales tax license before you make your first sale.

alt: Missouri Department of Revenue registration FAQ with the answer saying bonds are no longer required highlighted
caption: Since 2018, a new seller does not post a bond unless the Department asks for one.

alt: Missouri Department of Revenue Sales/Use Tax page with the sentence on the 4.225 percent state rate highlighted
caption: The state rate is 4.225%, and cities, counties and districts add local tax.

alt: Service New Brunswick Corporate Registry page with the Register a business name link highlighted
caption: Service New Brunswick's Corporate Registry registers the business names sole proprietors trade under. You only need it if you use a name other than your own.

alt: Service New Brunswick register or renew a business name page with the sentence on who must register highlighted
caption: Register your business name if you trade under any name other than your own. File within two months of starting.

alt: Service New Brunswick register or renew a business name page on the Fees tab with the Certificate of Business Name fee highlighted
caption: A Certificate of Business Name costs $112, including the $12 Royal Gazette fee. Renewing it every five years costs $62.

alt: City of Fredericton zoning and land use page with the question about having a home based business highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Fredericton, for example, allows a home occupation in a single detached house or mini-home, under its zoning by-law. Look up your own city or town in the same way.

alt: EDPNC Business Structure page with the Sole Proprietorship heading highlighted
caption: Read how a sole proprietorship works, the simplest way to start.

alt: NC Secretary of State limited liability company fees page with the Articles of Organization fee highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, note the $125 filing fee for Articles of Organization.

alt: NC Secretary of State Assumed Business Names FAQ with the answer on where to file highlighted
caption: File your assumed business name certificate with your county register of deeds.

alt: NC Secretary of State Maintaining Registration page with the LLC annual report due date highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, note that its annual report is due by April 15 each year, starting the year after you form it.

alt: NC Department of Revenue Sales and Use Tax Registration page with the Register Online link and the no fee notice highlighted
caption: Register online for a Certificate of Registration. There is no fee.

alt: NC Department of Revenue Current Sales and Use Tax Rates page with the note on the 4.75% state rate highlighted
caption: Look up the total state and local rate for each county you sell into.

alt: NC Department of Revenue Remote Sales page with the $100,000 remote seller threshold highlighted
caption: Sellers based outside North Carolina must register once their sales into the state pass $100,000 a year.

alt: EDPNC Business Licenses and Permits page with the note that North Carolina has no generic state business license highlighted
caption: North Carolina has no single state business license, so check the license directory for what you sell.

alt: NJ Division of Revenue Getting Registered page with the $100 formation fee highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, check the Certificate of Formation fee before you decide.

alt: NJ Division of Taxation sales tax page with the registration requirement for all sellers highlighted
caption: Register to collect sales tax, even if you sell only at flea markets or craft shows.

alt: NJ Division of Taxation sales tax page with the quarterly filing requirement highlighted
caption: File quarterly returns by the 20th of the month after each quarter.

alt: NJ Division of Taxation remote sellers page with the $100,000 economic threshold highlighted
caption: Out-of-state sellers register once they pass $100,000 or 200 sales into New Jersey.

alt: City of St. John's starting a business page with the link to its guide to municipal regulations for business highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. St. John's, for example, publishes a guide to the municipal regulations and permits that apply to businesses. Look up your own city or town in the same way.

alt: Nova Scotia choose a legal structure page with the sole proprietorship description highlighted
caption: Read Nova Scotia's guide to legal structures. A sole proprietorship is a business owned by one person and not incorporated.

alt: Nova Scotia register a sole proprietorship page with the $68.55 registration fee highlighted
caption: Reserve your name first, then register the sole proprietorship. Registration costs $68.55 and must be renewed every year for the same fee.

alt: Halifax home improvement permits page on the Home Based Business tab with the development permit requirement highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Halifax, for example, needs a development permit for a home-based business. Look up your own municipality in the same way.

alt: NWT Corporate Registries business names page on the entity types tab with the proprietorship description highlighted
caption: A proprietorship is owned by one person, with no legal distinction between you and the business, so you are personally liable.

alt: NWT Corporate Registries business names forms tab with the sole proprietorship forms highlighted
caption: Download the sole proprietorship forms and mail or deliver the signed originals. Reservation is $25 and registration $50.

alt: City of Yellowknife business licences page with the home based business application highlighted
caption: Every business in the Northwest Territories needs a licence. In Yellowknife, a home-based business applies for a City licence and development permit together.

alt: Nunavut Legal Registries partnerships and business names page with the 60-day registration rule and the fee schedule link highlighted
caption: Register a business name with Nunavut Legal Registries within 60 days of first using it. The fee is $50.

alt: NY Business Express Sole Proprietorship page with the sentence describing a sole proprietorship highlighted
caption: Read the Business Express overview of a sole proprietorship, the simplest way to start.

alt: NY Business Express LLC Articles of Organization page with the Required Fees section highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, check the filing and publication fees before you decide.

alt: NY Business Express Sole Proprietorship page with the assumed name filing fees highlighted
caption: Check the county clerk filing fee for your assumed name certificate.

alt: NY Business Express LLC Articles of Organization page with the newspaper publication requirement highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, read the newspaper publication requirement and its 120-day deadline.

alt: New York Tax Department Register as a sales tax vendor page with the Apply online button highlighted
caption: Apply online for a Certificate of Authority at least 20 days before you start selling.

alt: New York Tax Department Find sales tax rates page with the rate lookup by address button highlighted
caption: Look up the combined state and local rate for each delivery address.

alt: NY Business Express How to Start a Business page with the note on local permits and licenses highlighted
caption: Check with the local offices where you are based and where you sell for any local permits.

alt: Ontario page on choosing an ownership structure with the sole proprietorship section highlighted
caption: Read Ontario's guide to ownership structures. A sole proprietorship is the simplest way to start, but you are personally liable for the business.

alt: Ontario Business Registry page with the search link highlighted
caption: Search the Ontario Business Registry to check that no one else is already using the name you want.

alt: Ontario register your business online page with the email and card requirement and the sole proprietorship fee highlighted
caption: Check what you need before you start: a working email address and a debit or credit card. You create an Ontario.ca Login and an Ontario Business Account during set-up, and a sole proprietorship costs $60.

alt: Ontario page listing registration fees with the sole proprietorship new registration fee highlighted
caption: Registering a sole proprietorship online costs $60 and takes effect immediately. Renewing it every five years costs the same $60.

alt: City of Toronto business regulations page with the list of businesses that do not need a licence open and the retail stores item highlighted
caption: Each city sets its own rules. Toronto, for example, says retail stores selling new, non-food items do not need a municipal operating licence. Look up your own city or town's licensing page in the same way.

alt: Pennsylvania Department of State Fees page with the $125 Certificate of Organization fee for an LLC highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, check the Certificate of Organization fee before you decide.

alt: Pennsylvania Department of State LLC page with the sentence saying no advertising is required highlighted
caption: Unlike a fictitious name, forming a Pennsylvania LLC needs no newspaper ad.

alt: Pennsylvania Department of State Fictitious Names page with the sentence requiring registration with the Department of State highlighted
caption: A fictitious name is registered with the Pennsylvania Department of State, not your county.

alt: Pennsylvania Department of State Fees page with the $70 fictitious name registration fee highlighted
caption: Check the current fictitious name registration fee.

alt: Pennsylvania Department of State Fictitious Names page with the two-newspaper advertising rule highlighted
caption: Advertise the name in two newspapers in your county, one of them a legal newspaper.

alt: Pennsylvania Department of State Annual Reports page with the LLC filing dates row highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, file its annual report between January 1 and September 30.

alt: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue Register My Business for Taxes page with the Register Now button highlighted
caption: Register for your sales tax license through myPATH's online business tax registration.

alt: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue sales tax page with the 6 percent rate and local Allegheny and Philadelphia taxes highlighted
caption: The state rate is 6%, with 1% more in Allegheny County and 2% more in Philadelphia.

alt: PA Business One-Stop Shop Clothing Stores and Boutiques guide with the sentence saying there is no general business license highlighted
caption: Pennsylvania has no general business license, so check the licenses for your activity and your municipality.

alt: WordPress admin Products menu with Variation Converter and its Combine, Split and History tabs highlighted
caption: After you activate the plugin, open Products > Variation Converter. It has three tabs: Combine, Split and History.

alt: Variation Converter Combine tab after searching for Tee, with the search box, the ticked Classic Crew Tee group and the Combine into one product button highlighted
caption: Search for the product. Tick the groups and products that are one product, here the Classic Crew Tee group, and click Combine into one product. Pocket Tee Olive is a different shirt, so it stays unticked.

alt: Classic Crew Tee opened for review, with the Black label and the Create variable product button highlighted
caption: Check the new product: the label for each product, the attribute and the name. Untick any that don't belong, then click Create variable product.

alt: Variation Converter after creating the Classic Crew Tee variable product, with the success message highlighted
caption: The four tees are now one variable product with a Color option. The originals are hidden, not deleted, and Undo conversion puts them back.

alt: Classic Crew Tee product page in the shop with the Color menu highlighted
caption: In your shop, shoppers now see one Classic Crew Tee and pick a color from the menu.

alt: Variation Converter Split tab with the Canvas Apron variable product opened, its new product names and the Split button highlighted
caption: On the Split tab, open a variable product. Check the name each new product will get, untick any you don't want, then click Split into 2 simple products.

alt: All Products list with the new Canvas Apron Sand and Canvas Apron Charcoal simple products highlighted
caption: Each variation is now its own simple product with its SKU, price and stock. The variable product stays in your list but is hidden from the shop.

alt: Variation Converter History tab listing a combine and a split, with an Undo button highlighted
caption: History lists every conversion, newest first. Undo puts the products back the way they were.

alt: Québec.ca legal forms of enterprise page with the sentence saying a sole proprietorship has no legal existence separate from its owner highlighted
caption: Read Quebec's guide to legal forms. A sole proprietorship has no legal existence separate from you, so you are personally liable for its debts.

alt: Québec.ca about registration page with the rule on sole proprietorships that must register highlighted
caption: Register with the Registraire des entreprises if your business name doesn't include your first and last names. Registration costs $41.

alt: Montréal get an occupancy permit page for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal with the sentence about using part of your home for professional purposes highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. In Montréal, a certificate of occupancy is needed to use part of your home for professional purposes, and fees vary by borough. Check with your own municipality or borough.

alt: CRA business registration page with the Register with Business Registration Online link highlighted
caption: On the CRA business registration page, choose Register with Business Registration Online (BRO).

alt: CRA page listing ways to register for a business number and program accounts
caption: This section explains what a business number covers and which program accounts (like GST/HST) you can add to it.

alt: CRA GST/HST for businesses page with the Who needs to register section highlighted
caption: Check Who needs to register for GST/HST. Most businesses must register once taxable sales pass $30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters.

alt: CRA GST/HST for businesses page with the Get a GST/HST number and manage your account section highlighted
caption: When you're ready, open Get a GST/HST number and manage your account. Registration is done in Business Registration Online, signed in with your CRA account.

alt: IRS Get an employer identification number page with the Apply for an EIN button highlighted
caption: On the IRS EIN page, choose Apply for an EIN. Applying is free and takes one session.

alt: IRS Get an employer identification number page with the warning about sites that charge for an EIN highlighted
caption: Apply only on irs.gov. The IRS never charges for an EIN, so skip any site that asks for a fee.

alt: Streamlined Sales Tax Registration System page listing the member states, with the no-fee note highlighted
caption: If you reach a threshold in a Streamlined member state, you can register for several states at once here. The system itself is free.

alt: Saskatchewan Corporate Registry choose a business type page with the sole proprietorship option highlighted
caption: Read the Corporate Registry's guide to business types. A sole proprietorship is the simplest way to start.

alt: Saskatchewan Corporate Registry search and reserve a business name page with the name reservation expiry rule highlighted
caption: Reserve your business name before you register it. A reservation costs $50 and is held for 90 days.

alt: Government of Saskatchewan apply for a PST number page with the online new business registration through SETS highlighted
caption: Register for a PST vendor's licence online through Saskatchewan eTax Services (SETS).

alt: City of Saskatoon home-based business licence page with the $135 new licence fee highlighted
caption: Each municipality sets its own rules. Saskatoon, for example, charges $135 for a new home-based business licence and $95 a year to renew. Look up your own city or town in the same way.

alt: Tennessee Department of Revenue business set-up page with the sentence on sole proprietorship registration highlighted
caption: A sole proprietorship is registered under your own legal name, with your trade name added.

alt: Tennessee Department of Revenue franchise and excise tax page with the minimum franchise tax sentence highlighted
caption: An LLC also pays at least $100 a year in franchise tax.

alt: Tennessee Department of Revenue sales tax rates page with the 7% general rate sentence highlighted
caption: The state rate is 7% on most goods, and local rates add to it.

alt: Tennessee Department of Revenue resale certificate page with the sentence on automatic issue highlighted
caption: Your Certificate of Resale is issued automatically when you register.

alt: Tennessee Department of Revenue licenses page with the sentence on where to get a business license highlighted
caption: Get your business license from the county clerk and city clerk; each is $15.

alt: Tennessee Department of Revenue licenses page with the gross sales thresholds list highlighted
caption: Your yearly gross sales decide whether you need a minimum activity or standard license.

alt: Texas Secretary of State SOSPortal page with the $1.00 search fee highlighted
caption: Search business names on SOSPortal before you settle on one. Each search costs $1.

alt: Texas Secretary of State Form 205 instructions with the entity name and organizational designation rule highlighted
caption: Read the name rules before you form an LLC. The name needs an organizational designation that shows it is an LLC.

alt: Texas Secretary of State name filings FAQ with the answer on filing an assumed name certificate with the county clerk highlighted
caption: File your assumed name certificate with the county clerk in each county where you keep a business office. Ask the county clerk for the current fee.

alt: Texas Secretary of State Form 205 instructions with the $300 LLC filing fee highlighted
caption: Check the fee before you form an LLC. A certificate of formation costs $300.

alt: Texas Online Tax Registration Application page with the Apply for Permit via eSystems link highlighted
caption: Apply for your sales and use tax permit through eSystems. Allow 2–3 weeks to receive it.

alt: Texas Comptroller sales tax permit FAQ with the answer that there is no fee for the permit highlighted
caption: Note that the permit itself is free. You may be asked to post a security bond.

alt: Texas Business Permit Office page with the General Business License section highlighted
caption: Read the General Business License section. Texas has no general license, so check the licenses guide and your city and county instead.

alt: Virginia SCC LLC forms and fees page with the Form a new Virginia LLC (LLC1011) row and its $100 fee highlighted
caption: If you are weighing an LLC, check the SCC filing fee for Articles of Organization before you decide.

alt: Virginia SCC Business Entity Names FAQ with the rule on words an LLC name must include highlighted
caption: An LLC name must include "LLC" or a similar word, so check the SCC rule before you pick one.

alt: Virginia SCC Fictitious Names FAQ with the $10.00 filing fee highlighted
caption: Check the SCC filing fee for a fictitious name certificate, which sole proprietors file with the SCC too.

alt: Virginia SCC Annual Registration Fees FAQ with the Limited Liability Companies row showing the due date and $50.00 fee highlighted
caption: If you formed an LLC, note the yearly registration fee and that it is due by the end of your formation month.

alt: Virginia Tax Retail Sales and Use Tax page with the Register for sales tax online link highlighted
caption: Register with Virginia Tax for your Sales Tax Certificate of Registration before your first sale.

alt: Virginia Tax sales tax rates table with the 5.3% Everywhere else row highlighted
